item.text:
Continuation completed for Chapters 2B–8B. No scores, ranges, rankings, or judge advice were assigned. The repository remained read-only, so I could not persist the notebook or manifest; manifest-ready deltas are below.

### New evidence units

| ID | Evidence unit and locator | Limits | Chapter/lens mapping |
|---|---|---|---|
| E046 | Carnegie’s February 2022 review reports that the India–Pakistan ceasefire sharply reduced violations, with early-2022 reporting showing continued reduction; it documents improved conditions for border populations. [Carnegie, lines 53–65](https://carnegieendowment.org/research/2022/02/bordering-on-peace-evaluating-the-impact-of-the-india-pakistan-ceasefire) | Ceasefire was military-to-military and began in 2021; does not establish Modi’s personal direction or civilian-harm accountability. | 2B.1, 2B.2, 2B.4, 2B.6, 2B.10 |
| E047 | SIPRI’s 2022 arms-transfer fact sheet records India as a major arms importer and India as a modest exporter, with Myanmar, Sri Lanka, and Armenia among its 2017–21 recipients. [SIPRI fact sheet](https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2022-03/fs_2203_at_2021.pdf) | Mainly inherited/trajectory context; does not establish 2022 proxy conduct or unlawful transfers. | 2B.3, 2B.8, 2B.10 |
| E048 | HRW reported that Indian authorities in J&K restricted expression and assembly, intensified media/civil-society pressure, and failed to investigate alleged security-force abuses. [HRW, lines 607–628](https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/08/02/india-repression-persists-jammu-and-kashmir) | Stronger for government/security-authority attribution than personal Modi attribution; security threats and militant violence are also present. | 3B.1, 3B.4, 3B.5, 3B.8, 3B.10 |
| E049 | The Press Council of India’s 2022 annual report records 290 complaints against government, police, or individuals for attacks on press freedom, 27 press releases, and 672 matters disposed during the year. [Press Council report, PDF pp. 24–25](https://presscouncil.nic.in/WriteReadData/PDF/AnnualReport2022.pdf) | Shows institutional scrutiny and complaint visibility, not verified prevalence or central-government culpability for each complaint. | 3B.1, 3B.8, 3B.10; 4B.6, 4B.9 |
| E050 | India’s External Affairs Ministry rejected OHCHR criticism of the June 2022 arrest of Teesta Setalvad and two former police officers, asserting established judicial process; OHCHR called for release. [Hindustan Times, lines 109–136](https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-dismisses-criticism-of-teesta-setalvad-s-arrest-by-un-human-rights-agency-101656497580486.html) | Records competing official and external positions; does not independently resolve legality or Modi’s personal direction. | 3B.5, 3B.8, 3B.10; 4B.6, 4B.9 |
| E051 | The ECI’s 2022 statistical report documents assembly elections in Goa, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, and Uttarakhand, including turnout, party results, election petitions, disciplinary cases, seizures, and paid-news cases. [ECI report, PDF pp. 14–18](https://www.eci.gov.in/eci-backend/public/api/download?url=LMAhAK6sOPBp%2FNFF0iRfXbEB1EVSLT41NNLRjYNJJP1KivrUxbfqkDatmHy12e%2FzVx8fLfn2ReU7TfrqYobgItVaDT1%2FN9NoActktqO4y0Ti6YTNhJb3duBnsypGrGbsFOwC3iVoQ82MxhlUAMbtgRkU2VvXw6n8RkOkaSlgUgdOo00ndBxGzBsC%2B0pwZ4d5) | Establishes electoral administration and contestation, not a direct observer judgment on fairness or Modi’s national conduct. | 4B.1, 4B.2, 4B.4, 4B.8, 4B.10 |
| E052 | Freedom House assessed India’s executive selection procedures as generally free and fair and described private media as somewhat vigorous and diverse, while also documenting intensified pressure on critics and journalists. [Freedom House, lines 84–105, 164–169](https://freedomhouse.org/country/india/freedom-world/2022) | Comparative assessment; its favorable and adverse findings must be retained together rather than collapsed into one direction. | 4B.1, 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.9, 4B.10 |
| E053 | The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs reported 16 bills passed from April–November 2022, 60 committee meetings, and 73 parliamentary committee nominations. [PIB, lines 13–15, 63–81](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1887684) | Official administrative account; does not establish legislative independence or quality of scrutiny. | 4B.4, 4B.8, 8B.3 |
| E054 | An IMF 2022 working paper estimated that food transfers kept extreme poverty low during the pandemic and reduced post-transfer consumption inequality; the analysis covers through 2020–21, so it is persistent context rather than a 2022 event. [IMF, lines 260–285](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/wp/issues/2022/04/05/pandemic-poverty-and-inequality-evidence-from-india-516155) | Does not establish 2022 household distribution, job quality, or Modi-specific causation. | 5B.2, 5B.4, 5B.6, 5B.9 |
| E055 | The CAG records that Report No. 31 of 2022, a financial audit of Union Government accounts, was tabled on 21 December 2022. [CAG report record, lines 184–207](https://cag.gov.in/en/audit-report/details/117818) | Establishes an audit and oversight channel, not a finding of corruption or personal misconduct. | 5B.8, 7B.4, 8B.3, 8B.8 |
| E056 | A parliamentary committee in April 2022 summoned CAG officials over delays in laying audited accounts from more than 1,000 autonomous bodies and PSUs, while describing parliamentary scrutiny of public expenditure. [Indian Express, lines 69–123](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/cag-audit-report-delays-7851473/) | Indicates oversight friction and corrective institutional action; no personal Modi nexus. | 5B.8, 7B.4, 8B.3, 8B.8 |
| E057 | The World Bank’s June 2022 financing approved two $500 million loans supporting PM-ABHIM, health-system reform, surveillance, pathogen detection, primary care, quality measurement, and state-specific workforce strategies. [World Bank, lines 34–49](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/06/28/world-bank-approves-1-billion-to-support-india-s-health-sector-for-pandemic-preparedness-and-enhanced-health-service-del) | Documents program mechanisms and external financing, not completed outcomes; implementation is shared between center and states. | 6B.1, 6B.2, 6B.4, 6B.5, 6B.6, 6B.10; 8B.1, 8B.2, 8B.3, 8B.6 |
| E058 | The parliamentary health committee found fragile infrastructure, health-worker shortages, poor initial rural vaccination, oxygen mismanagement, reduced testing, and opaque vaccine-approval procedures. [PRS, lines 95–110](https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/vaccine-development-distribution-management-and-mitigation-of-pandemic-covid-19) | Retrospective and partly earlier-period evidence; attribution is institutional and shared, not personal. | 6B.2, 6B.4, 6B.5, 6B.6, 6B.8; 8B.6, 8B.7, 8B.8 |
| E059 | The same committee recommended auditing COVID deaths associated with oxygen shortages and compensating affected families; it reported inadequate identification of oxygen-related deaths and uneven oxygen distribution. [Indian Express, lines 110–146](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/audit-deaths-due-to-oxygen-shortage-during-covid-second-wave-8149422/) | Important contrary and corrective evidence, but the committee did not establish a complete causal death count. | 6B.2, 6B.5, 6B.8; 8B.6, 8B.8 |
| E060 | The Supreme Court’s 24 June 2022 judgment dismissed Zakia Jafri’s challenge concerning alleged larger conspiracy in the 2002 Gujarat violence and upheld the procedural disposition of the SIT investigation. [Supreme Court judgment, pp. 1–10 and 140–141](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/34207/34207_2018_3_1502_36189_Judgement_24-Jun-2022.pdf) | Post-event judicial disposition relevant to 2022 integrity context, but not proof of universal exculpation or present-period integrity. | 3B.7, 4B.5, 7B.1, 7B.2, 7B.7 |
| E061 | The Supreme Court judgment records that the complaint alleged high-level conspiracy, while the court described the complaint as vague and noted contradictions with contemporaneous records. [Judgment, PDF pp. 140–141](https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/34207/34207_2018_3_1502_36189_Judgement_24-Jun-2022.pdf) | This is a judicial characterization of historical allegations, not a finding about 2022 conduct or personal honesty generally. | 7B.1, 7B.2, 7B.7 |
| E062 | The 2022 Electoral Commission report provides target-year records of election petitions, disciplinary cases, seizures, and paid-news cases, creating recoverable institutional-integrity leads but no personal Modi nexus. [ECI report, PDF pp. 166–172](https://www.eci.gov.in/eci-backend/public/api/download?url=LMAhAK6sOPBp%2FNFF0iRfXbEB1EVSLT41NNLRjYNJJP1KivrUxbfqkDatmHy12e%2FzVx8fLfn2ReU7TfrqYobgItVaDT1%2FN9NoActktqO4yTi6YTNhJb3duBnsypGRbsFOwC3iVoQ82MxhlUAMbtgRkU2VvXw6n8RkOkaSlgUgdOo00ndBxGzBsC%2B0pwZ4d5) | Requires case-level follow-up; not counted as personal-integrity evidence by itself. | 7B.3, 7B.4, 7B.8 |
| E063 | The World Bank describes PM-ABHIM as a center–state program with explicit surveillance, pathogen detection, quality-certification, household-access, and workforce mechanisms. [World Bank, lines 40–49](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/06/28/world-bank-approves-1-billion-to-support-india-s-health-sector-for-pandemic-preparedness-and-enhanced-health-service-del) | Program architecture is not evidence of realized portfolio effectiveness. | 8B.1, 8B.2, 8B.3, 8B.6 |
| E064 | The IMF food-transfer analysis supplies an independent outcome-oriented check on the welfare portfolio, finding substantial pandemic-era poverty and inequality protection through transfers. [IMF, lines 260–264](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/wp/issues/2022/04/05/pandemic-poverty-and-inequality-evidence-from-india-516155) | Coverage ends in 2020–21 and cannot substitute for 2022 implementation evaluation. | 8B.2, 8B.6, 8B.7 |
| E065 | The 2022 parliamentary health findings provide portfolio-level contrary evidence: implementation weaknesses, oxygen failures, rural vaccination gaps, and insufficient vaccine transparency. [PRS, lines 98–110](https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/vaccine-development-distribution-management-and-mitigation-of-pandemic-covid-19) | One health portfolio, not a complete assessment of Modi’s wider governing portfolio. | 8B.6, 8B.7, 8B.8 |
| E066 | The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs reported committee activity, public-grievance disposal, and monitoring systems during 2022. [PIB, lines 63–81](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1887684) | Official performance account; requires independent corroboration and does not establish durable effectiveness. | 8B.3, 8B.4, 8B.8 |

### Chapter handoff

- **2B:** Improved modestly through ceasefire and border-population evidence. Civilian harm, Pakistan diplomacy, proxy conduct, and military accountability remain substantial gaps. The chapter remains thin.
- **3B:** Improved with direct 2022 HRW material, Press Council complaint/disposition records, and the government’s response to OHCHR. Attribution remains stronger for Indian authorities than for Modi personally; state-level and security-force conduct must remain separated.
- **4B:** ECI records establish functioning electoral administration and contestation; Freedom House provides both favorable and adverse institutional evidence. Direct observer evidence, legislative independence, appointments, and transfer/term-limit conduct remain incomplete.
- **5B:** Independent IMF distributional analysis and CAG oversight records add useful context, but target-year household distribution, job quality, procurement, capture, and flagship-program evaluation remain unresolved.
- **6B:** This chapter gained the strongest new material: World Bank program architecture plus parliamentary findings and oxygen-accountability recommendations. Regional/group equity, affordability, service quality, and center–state responsibility remain undercovered.
- **7B:** The bounded contrary search recovered a target-period Supreme Court disposition and institutional election/audit leads. No defensible personal knowledge, direction, benefit, tolerance, or obstruction nexus was established. Integrity evidence remains insufficient for personal attribution.
- **8B:** Program mechanisms, independent welfare analysis, parliamentary criticism, and administrative oversight now provide a more balanced effectiveness base. Independent outcome attribution, adaptation, correction, durability, and portfolio-wide coverage remain weak.

### Manifest-ready changes

All E046–E066 should be added with the exact `methodology_ids` shown above and disposition `final_evidence`, except:

- **E047:** `final_evidence` with an explicit inherited/trajectory-context limitation.
- **E062:** `discovery_only` unless the underlying election-petition, seizure, or paid-news case records are separately opened and analyzed.
- **E060–E061:** `final_evidence` only as a judicial disposition of historical allegations, not as general exculpatory evidence.
- No existing item was rejected or renumbered.
- Existing E029 remains `corroborative_duplicate`; E036 remains `discovery_only`; E037 remains `rejected`.

The recoverable continuation work for Chapters 2B–8B was attempted. Remaining gaps are evidence and attribution limitations, not negative ruler evidence.
